![fig-1](gce-al-pm-mechanics-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

The curve with the equation $y = 2x(3-x)$ crosses the $x$-axis at $O$ and $B$.

figures.legende: Sketch (not to scale) of the parabola y = 2x(3 - x) through O and B on the x-axis, with a straight line meeting the y-axis at E, cutting the curve at C and D; A is the foot of the vertical from C to the x-axis; R is the region between the curve and the line DE.

incertitudes: Question 6 : le point O du sujet est l'origine (0, 0) ; le point A (pied de la verticale issue de C) n'est pas nomme dans le texte, seulement sur la figure.
Question 6 (b) : le sujet dit « Show that the value of k is 5/2 » sans preciser que k est non nul ; le corrige utilise que D est distinct de O (D est a droite de C sur la figure).

questions.enonce_markdown: State the coordinates of the point $B$. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The curve meets the $x$-axis where $y = 0$: $2x(3 - x) = 0$, so $x = 0$ (the point $O$) or $x = 3$.

$$\boxed{B = (3, 0)}$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
A straight line, which crosses the $y$-axis at the point $E$ with coordinates $(0, 5)$, meets the curve at the points $C$ and $D$, as shown in the diagram above. The coordinates of the point $D$ are $(k, k)$.

Show that the value of $k$ is $\dfrac{5}{2}$. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
$D = (k, k)$ lies on the curve $y = 2x(3-x)$, so

$$k = 2k(3 - k).$$

$D$ is not the origin $O$ (it is the point on the right of the curve in the diagram, with $k > 0$), so $k \neq 0$ and we may divide by $k$:

$$1 = 2(3 - k) = 6 - 2k \;\Longrightarrow\; 2k = 5 \;\Longrightarrow\; k = \frac52. \qquad \blacksquare$$

So $D = \left(\tfrac52, \tfrac52\right)$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find an equation of the straight line passing through $D$ and $E$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
$E = (0, 5)$ and $D = \left(\tfrac52, \tfrac52\right)$. The gradient is

$$m = \frac{\tfrac52 - 5}{\tfrac52 - 0} = \frac{-\tfrac52}{\tfrac52} = -1.$$

The line cuts the $y$-axis at $E$, so the intercept is $5$:

$$\boxed{y = 5 - x \quad (\text{equivalently } x + y = 5)}$$

Check with $D$: $5 - \tfrac52 = \tfrac52$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the $x$-coordinates of the point $C$ is $1$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
$C$ and $D$ are the points where the line $y = 5 - x$ meets the curve $y = 2x(3-x)$. Equate:

$$2x(3 - x) = 5 - x \;\Longrightarrow\; 6x - 2x^2 = 5 - x \;\Longrightarrow\; 2x^2 - 7x + 5 = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; (x - 1)(2x - 5) = 0.$$

So $x = 1$ or $x = \dfrac52$. The root $x = \dfrac52$ is the point $D$ (part (b)), therefore the other intersection $C$ has

$$\boxed{x_C = 1}$$

(and $y_C = 5 - 1 = 4$, which agrees with $2(1)(3 - 1) = 4$, so $C = (1, 4)$.) $\blacksquare$

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the area of the region $R$ bounded by the curve $y = 2x(3-x)$ and line $DE$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Between $x = 1$ ($C$) and $x = \dfrac52$ ($D$) the curve lies above the line (for example at $x = 2$: curve $y = 4$, line $y = 3$). So

$$\text{Area} = \int_1^{5/2}\bigl[2x(3-x) - (5 - x)\bigr]\,dx = \int_1^{5/2}\left(-2x^2 + 7x - 5\right)dx.$$

An antiderivative is $F(x) = -\dfrac{2x^3}{3} + \dfrac{7x^2}{2} - 5x$.

$$F\!\left(\tfrac52\right) = -\frac{2}{3}\cdot\frac{125}{8} + \frac72\cdot\frac{25}{4} - \frac{25}{2} = -\frac{125}{12} + \frac{175}{8} - \frac{25}{2} = \frac{-250 + 525 - 300}{24} = -\frac{25}{24},$$

$$F(1) = -\frac23 + \frac72 - 5 = \frac{-4 + 21 - 30}{6} = -\frac{13}{6} = -\frac{52}{24}.$$

$$\text{Area} = F\!\left(\tfrac52\right) - F(1) = -\frac{25}{24} + \frac{52}{24} = \frac{27}{24}$$

$$\boxed{\text{Area of } R = \tfrac98 \text{ square units} = 1.125}$$

Check by the standard result for the area between a parabola with leading coefficient $a$ and a chord: $\dfrac{|a|}{6}(x_2 - x_1)^3 = \dfrac{2}{6}\left(\dfrac32\right)^3 = \dfrac13 \cdot \dfrac{27}{8} = \dfrac98$.
